answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a single attested device key that can only earn one reputation track, like a ferry that may dock at just one wharf along a river: a fake fleet must buy real hardware for every copy, and its cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once. Work history then climbs a ridge of completed, peer-checked jobs, so new identities start with zero trust and an attacker cannot clone a good record cheaply.
